abstract: Probabilistic discrete-range models, including dispersal-extinction-cladogenesis (DEC), DIVALIKE, BAYAREALIKE, founder-event speciation (+J), spatial modifiers, and time stratification, underpin historical biogeography. As empirical datasets grow, however, BioGeoBEARS workflows face slow multi-area optimization and branch-wise rejection stochastic mapping that fails on rare stepping-stone pathways and scales poorly across posterior trees. Standard fixed-tree pruning likelihoods also retain an absorbing null range without conditioning on extant tip survival, which often drives extinction estimates toward zero and inflates founder-event support, whereas DEC* avoids null absorption only by forbidding single-area extirpation. Boundary Hessian failures and single-tree point estimates also leave parameter, model, phylogenetic, and mapping uncertainties unquantified. Here we present RustBEARS, a Rust engine with BioGeoBEARS-compatible R and Python packages. Across 1,339 configurations from 77 studies, RustBEARS matches BioGeoBEARS log-likelihoods (median |delta lnL| = 9.95 x 10^-14) and ancestral probabilities (<= 1.50 x 10^-14), accelerates 64- to 256-state optimization 2.8- to 17.3-fold on one core and 4.1- to 36.1-fold on eight cores over the fastest BioGeoBEARS setting, and replaces trial-limited rejection with Uniformization stochastic mapping (170.9-fold median speedup for 200-map Python runs across 30 studies). RustBEARS also introduces whole-tree tip-survival conditioning for unstratified and chronologically emerging island models alongside five frequentist uncertainty tools. Across 58 extant clades from this 77-study archive, survival conditioning cuts near-zero DEC extinction estimates from 62.1% to 0.0% (87.9% finite interior, 12.1% ceiling-censored) and lowers AICc preference for DEC+J from 75.9% to 36.2%.
